primarySource.citation: Cong, T. L., Bedjanian, E. and Dagaut, P. (2010), Oxidation of ethylene and propene in the presence of CO2 and H2O: Experimental and detailed kinetic modeling study, Combustion Science and Technology 182, 333-349.

benchmarks.measurementBasis: Molar ppm on the basis stored by ReSpecTh; no dry or reference-O2 correction is applied.

uncertainty.details: ReSpecTh labels these species-specific values as estimated standard deviations combining scatter and estimated uncertainty. They are not claimed as uncertainties reported by the primary paper.

primarySource.citation: Aul, C. J., Metcalfe, W. K., Burke, S. M., Curran, H. J. and Petersen, E. L. (2013), Ignition and kinetic modeling of methane and ethane fuel blends with oxygen: A design of experiments approach, Combustion and Flame 160, 1153-1167.

benchmarks.ignitionDefinition: Time from the post-shock initial state to the maximum pressure-rise rate, matching the ReSpecTh ignitionType target p and type d/dt max.
benchmarks.measurementBasis: Reported shock-tube ignition delay in microseconds at each reported post-shock temperature and pressure; the comparison uses an adiabatic constant-volume reactor and the maximum pressure-rise rate without fitting.

uncertainty.details: ReSpecTh stores an estimated relative evaluated standard deviation for every delay. Absolute microsecond uncertainties below are the reported delay multiplied by that relative value; they are not claimed as primary-paper reported uncertainties.

dataSource.attribution: Chemical Kinetics Laboratory, Institute of Chemistry, Eotvos Lorand University, Budapest, Hungary; ReSpecTh file DOI 10.24388/x10004030.
dataSource.modification: Mixture 4 was transcribed from XML into this catalog; pressure was converted from atm to Pa and each relative evaluated standard deviation was also expressed as an absolute microsecond uncertainty.

benchmarks.limitation: This high-temperature, dilute, near-atmospheric methane shock-tube series qualifies only the declared zero-dimensional ignition-delay comparison. Its 1686-2248 K range exceeds the 800-1500 K range described by the CRECK-S deposit, so it is explicit extrapolation evidence rather than validation inside that stated range. It does not qualify flame speed, C2/C3/C4 chemistry, fired-heater mixing or heat transfer, emissions reporting, or plant behavior.

mechanisms.validity: Candidate for C1-C4 finite-rate oxidation studies. The deposit describes validation over 800-1500 K, atmospheric pressure and equivalence ratios 0.5-2.0, but the companion paper is still in revision. This record does not establish heater or emissions qualification.
mechanisms.limitation: Evidence in this catalog is limited to one lean C2 ethylene JSR series and one high-temperature C1 methane ignition-delay series that lies above the deposit's stated temperature range. Licensed C3/C4 observations with uncertainty remain required.
